children: HelloFresh shares dropped after the German meal-kit company warned it added fewer customers than anticipated during its back-to-school campaign, prompting third-quarter results to miss expectations and a cut to its full-year outlook.
Shares in HelloFresh were down 13% in early European morning trading Friday, adding to losses earlier in the year that meant the stock has shed nearly two-thirds of its value since the start of 2026.
The company said it expected both revenue and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the third quarter to fall short of analysts' expectations.

It projects third-quarter revenue to decline by between 11% and 12% excluding currency changes, against the 6.8% decline anticipated by the average of analysts' forecasts. Quarterly adjusted Ebitda is forecast to range from 45 million to 55 million euros ($51.2 million-$62.6 million) at constant currency, below the consensus among analysts of 57.2 million euros.

HelloFresh said marketing-spending cuts during the third quarter meant the back-to-school period didn't lead to the volume of new customers required to meet its latest guidance and current market expectations. Reductions in marketing spending were more pronounced in the third quarter than in the first half, it added.

As a result, the company lowered its expectations for 2026 revenue, guiding for a decline of between 9% and 11% excluding currency changes. It had previously said it anticipated a drop at the bottom end of the 3% to 6% range.
HelloFresh also cut its annual guidance for adjusted Ebitda to between 350 million and 370 million euros at constant currency, from a range of 375 million to 425 million euros previously.

The company had cautioned that its revenue guidance hinged on the success of its back-to-school campaign while signaling confidence in its earnings outlook, so the profit warning will further undermine investor confidence in its ability to reach ambitious targets, analysts at J.P. Morgan wrote in a note to clients.
